svg.text: S4 AISLE SHUTTLE — the J-hook and the runner strips
A hook without a motor: the whole carriage moves 5 mm up or down to catch or release a box rim.
hook: 0 motors, 0 wires (engaged by Z ± 5 mm)
pull force ≤ 30 N, measured by the Y motor current

g.text: 1 Catch and pull (section at the box end)
rack face
box
carriage runner
← beam
carriage comes down
(a) runners 5 mm low: tip 2 mm below the seat
(b) carriage +5 mm: tip 3 mm up in the seat
(c) hook pulls: the tip drags the downturned rim
2 Runner strips across a lane (seen from the aisle)
176 rim · 179 clear · 158 body
partition (ladder, 1.5 mm)
Each lane has a runner strip
welded to each partition at every
level. The box hangs by its two
side rims; nothing is under it,
so spills drain to the tray.
Orange outline: the carriage’s own
runners, in front of the slot.
carriage arrives 5 mm low
pull: carriage runners 0.5 mm BELOW
push: carriage runners 0.5 mm ABOVE
so the box always steps DOWN;
2 mm × 30° lead-ins absorb ± 1.5 mm
3 Along a runner: far tab, near bump, step down
far tab
rack runner, 182 long
bump 0.8
+ lead-in
carriage runner, 0.5 lower
at rest: the bump keeps the box from creeping out
pull: the rim rides over the bump (≈ 2 N), then steps down
on the carriage
push back until the far rim meets the tab
at rest
heights of tab, bump and steps drawn 4× exaggerated
4 Lift-off and put-away: the hook needs no release
rear slot
carriage
tab
lift-off: the rim rises away from the tip — nothing to release
put-away: box set down, the tip lands in the seat by itself
push 167 mm until the far rim meets the tab
carriage −5 mm: the tip drops out, the hook retracts
